candidates.title: Then there is prompt injection, a malicious email, ...: The Wild Wide West of OpenClaw Agentic System Security

candidates.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
candidates.summary: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following injected instructions. We evaluate HoS on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B. We compare it against SecAlign++, a state-of-the-art finetuning-based defense, and ASIDE, a defense that, like ours, builds instruction-data separation into the model architecture. candidates.title: After the Attacker Leaves: Benchmarking Carryover Attacks on LLM Agents
candidates.summary: Modern LLM agents persist state across sessions via two channels: long-lived memory files silently prepended to the system prompt, and scheduled tasks waking the agent without user input. A one-time indirect prompt injection committed to either channel can re-fire across sessions long after the attacker leaves, threats we term carryover attacks. Existing prompt-injection benchmarks evaluate attacks only in the session where malicious content is first observed, leaving the gate governing when and how often a planted payload later re-fires unmeasured. candidates.title: Agentic AI Architectures: A Survey of Patterns, Memory Systems, and Protocols
candidates.summary: AI agents have grown dramatically more capable — planning over futures, calling tools, remembering across sessions, coordinating in teams — while the data they act upon remains ungoverned, untested, and uninspected. This survey argues that AI agents are as good as their data foundations: an agent’s capability ceiling in production is set not by its language model but by the quality, governance, freshness, and semantic structure of the data it perceives and acts upon. candidates.title: WAAA! Web Adversaries Against Web Agents
candidates.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into web browsers to create agentic browsing systems that execute actions on behalf of the user. Prior work considering the security of agentic browsers focuses on indirect prompt-injection attacks. candidates.title: When AI Agents Go Off Script: How Websites Become Targets
candidates.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
candidates.summary: An AI agent goes off script when it does something its owner did not intend. That happens in three ways. Someone else writes the script, by planting instructions in a page, email or tool the agent reads. An attacker runs the agent, and points its speed at your website. Or the agent misreads its own task and acts on the mistake. Websites sit in the middle of all three. They are where attacking agents probe for accounts and records, and they are where hidden instructions wait for the agents that browse them. The evidence is no longer theoretical.
